rationale: Map handoff for the confirmed recovery finding. Three map objects are clarified with sources: Behavior B9 records that the recovering replica announces the newly made ballot as its own VBallot, Behavior B11 records that the running maximum therefore skips remote values at older vbals together with the confirmed observation, and core_overview's context explanation carries the sourced conditional relationship instead of an intent-only description. No requirement, binding, edge or identity changes; the confirmed claim and its checks remain the primary home for the finding.

B9-recovery-trigger.rationale: A sourced branch was added for the ballot/vbal the recovering replica publishes, and the unknown that asked whether the local record is a sufficient seed is replaced by the honest residual: the checks fix the resolution and accept rounds, while the timeout trigger and a real commit round are unread.
B9-recovery-trigger.preserves: The trigger, guards, writes, fact relations and the execution-timeout recovery path are unchanged; only what the entry publishes and the remaining unread history are updated.

B11-prepare-resolution.rationale: The selection rule's effect is now described: the candidate is the last reply at or above the running maximum, and the self entry has already raised that maximum to the new ballot, which the direct check confirmed can end in a NOOP vector for an instance another replica committed.
B11-prepare-resolution.preserves: The highest-vbal rule, the sub-case dispatch and the dead sub-case finding are unchanged; the addition is a sourced description of the implemented behaviour.

core_overview.rationale: The context explanation no longer reads as intent only: it records the sourced conditional relationship (own vbal raised to the new ballot, older remote values skipped) and the confirmed in-scope consequence.
core_overview.preserves: Formation, connection and all behavior and fact references are unchanged.

feedback.answered: The recovery consequence is established rather than hypothesised. The trusted runner reproduced, and a fresh correspondence review accepted, three linked observations on the same obligation: the resolution does not adopt a reply that reports the instance COMMITTED (adopted_committed false); the accept round it starts nevertheless completes (accept_oks 0 to 1) and the recoverer commits a NOOP vector for that instance (vectors_match false against the peer's PUT); and after the recoverer's Commit broadcast the disagreement survives, with the already-committed replica keeping PUT while the recoverer and a third replica hold NOOP (all_committed_match false). The map now records the mechanism that produces this in B9, B11 and the core overview: the recovering replica publishes the newly made ballot as its own VBallot, so the running maximum used by element.VBallot >= lb.ballot skips values at older vbals.
remaining: whether executing the instances makes the disagreement visible in applied state rather than only in the committed records (the checks do not run the state machine)
whether the execution-timeout trigger and a real proposal/commit round reach the same recovering-replica state (the checks use a prepared COMMITTED record and enter recovery directly)

whether the accept-phase status omission changes the same recovery decision, since an accept-only acceptor reports accepted attributes with Status NONE and no command at the accepted vbal (S11-handleAccept, S15-handlePrepareReply)
feedback.rationale: The finding now has a confirmed claim, three reviewed checks and a fresh map description, so the next useful work is a different responsibility or an explicit consequence step rather than more variants of this scenario. The map handoff replaces the answered seed question with its residual and records the mechanism where the protocol is described, keeping the claim and checks as the home for the verdict.
